overall: The AG found the Wayland School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law on all three allegations: late response to a minutes request, an omitted document in open session minutes, and insufficiently detailed revised executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested revised executive session minutes on July 7, 2015; the committee did not respond until after a renewed request, about 21 days later.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee did not respond to the complainant's request until 21 days later, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law for failing to provide the minutes within 10 days of a request.

allegations.summary: The May 26, 2015 open session minutes omitted the August 28, 2014 executive session minutes, which were amended and released as a document used at that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Open Meeting Law requires that documents used during the meeting be included in the minutes, we find that the Committee violated the Law by omitting this information from its minutes.

allegations.summary: Revised August 28, 2014 executive session minutes, ordered in OML 2015-55, still omitted the name of the parent whose email was discussed, so they lacked sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to sufficiently revise its August 28, 2014 minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Further revise the August 28, 2014 executive session minutes in accordance with the guidance in the determination.
Complete Open Meeting Law training conducted by an approved attorney or organization and certify to the AG's office within 30 days that it has complied.
remedy_passage: we order the Committee to further revise its August 28, 2014 executive session minutes in accordance with our guidance above.
